1oce16o.q: If a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must remove the load, if possible.
1oce16o.why: A driver whose load falls must remove it where possible and clear the road as quickly as possible.

8q13yj.q: On an extra-urban road, if a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must give advance warning of the obstacle with the stopped-vehicle sign (triangle).
8q13yj.why: Outside built-up areas the obstacle must be warned of in advance with the warning triangle (segnale mobile triangolare di pericolo).

1raukeo.q: If a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must promptly clear the way for traffic as far as possible.
1raukeo.why: The driver must clear the road for traffic as quickly as possible.

k4uwy9.q: If a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must give advance warning of the obstacle with the STOP sign.
k4uwy9.why: The STOP sign is a priority sign and is not used to warn of obstacles. The warning triangle (triangolo mobile di pericolo) is used instead.

bvkqhc.q: If a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must stay in the vehicle and wait for rescue.
bvkqhc.why: The driver must act at once: remove the obstruction, clear the road and warn other traffic. Waiting passively for help is not allowed.

46py5e.q: If a vehicle breakdown obstructs the carriageway, the driver must promptly clear the way for approaching traffic.
46py5e.why: After a breakdown the driver must quickly free the road for approaching traffic.

siesut.q: If a vehicle breakdown obstructs the carriageway, the driver must push the vehicle off the carriageway or, if that is not possible, place it at the right-hand edge of the carriageway.
siesut.why: A broken-down vehicle must be pushed off the carriageway or, if that is impossible, placed at the right edge (margine destro).

pal2m8.q: If a fallen load or any other cause obstructs the carriageway, the driver must remove the obstruction, as far as possible.
pal2m8.why: Whatever the cause of the obstruction, the driver must remove it as far as possible.

1gufu4b.q: On an extra-urban road, if an accident obstructs the carriageway with damaged vehicles that cannot be removed, the driver or passengers must give advance warning of the area with the mobile triangular warning sign.
1gufu4b.why: Outside built-up areas, if damaged vehicles cannot be removed, the area must be marked in advance with the warning triangle.

ub237k.q: If a vehicle breakdown obstructs the carriageway, the driver does not have to move it while waiting for rescue if traffic is light.
ub237k.why: The duty to clear the road always applies, even when traffic is light.

196396d.q: If a fallen load obstructs the carriageway, the driver must avoid moving it so that the event can be accurately reconstructed.
196396d.why: The obstruction must be removed where possible; it is not left in place to reconstruct events.

1tcbuwv.q: If a vehicle breakdown obstructs the carriageway and the vehicle cannot be moved, the driver must inform the police, without having to give advance warning of the area.
1tcbuwv.why: Besides informing the police, the driver must also give appropriate advance warning of the area.

h0zhmt.q: If a fallen load that cannot be removed obstructs the carriageway, the driver may avoid informing the police if he warns the area in advance with effective hand signals.
h0zhmt.why: If the load cannot be removed, the police must be informed and the area warned in advance; hand signals do not replace informing the police (organo di polizia).

1ronziv.q: Anyone who could not avoid the fall or spillage of slippery, flammable or otherwise dangerous materials must, among other things, give advance warning of the area with the mobile danger sign, even in the middle of the carriageway.
1ronziv.why: The mobile danger sign may be placed even in the middle of the carriageway to warn of the area.

rq7ce5.q: Anyone who could not avoid the fall or spillage of dangerous materials must, among other things, give hand signals to stop vehicles from the side where the mobile danger sign has not been placed.
rq7ce5.why: Hand signals must be given on the side where the mobile sign is not placed, to stop vehicles passing.

1egxvtb.q: Anyone who could not avoid the fall or spillage of slippery, flammable or dangerous materials must, among other things, remove them or, if possible, spread sand, earth, sawdust or other suitable material to restore grip.
1egxvtb.why: The person responsible must remove the substance or, if possible, spread sand, earth or sawdust to restore grip (aderenza).

11zj48q.q: On an extra-urban road, anyone who could not avoid the fall or spillage of slippery, flammable or otherwise dangerous materials must, among other things, give advance warning of the area with the mobile danger sign, placed even in the middle of the carriageway.
11zj48q.why: The mobile danger sign may be placed even in the middle of the carriageway to warn of the area.

1j0u1pw.q: A motor vehicle driver who could not avoid a spillage of dangerous materials may skip giving advance warning of the area with the mobile danger sign if he uses sound signals to keep other vehicles away.
1j0u1pw.why: Sound signals never replace the mobile danger sign, which must always be placed.

qqtkn4.q: Anyone who could not avoid the fall of slippery materials must divert traffic while waiting for the road owner to restore optimal conditions.
qqtkn4.why: The person must warn in advance and remove or neutralise the materials. Diverting traffic is not the duty.

1txwi1u.q: Anyone who could not avoid the fall or spillage of dangerous materials must, among other things, give hand signals to warn of the danger only on the side where the mobile triangular danger sign has been placed.
1txwi1u.why: Hand signals are given on the side where the mobile sign is not placed, not on the side where it is.

1fvtwrc.q: Outside built-up areas, at night, when the rear position or emergency lights are missing or insufficient, it is mandatory to give advance warning of a vehicle stopped on the carriageway with the mobile triangular danger sign.
1fvtwrc.why: Outside built-up areas at night, the triangle is mandatory when rear lights are missing or insufficient.

oeudve.q: Outside built-up areas, at night, it is mandatory to give advance warning with the mobile triangular danger sign of any load accidentally fallen from the vehicle onto the carriageway.
oeudve.why: Outside built-up areas at night, a fallen load must always be warned of with the warning triangle.

12w6w9b.q: Outside built-up areas, it is mandatory even by day to give advance warning of a vehicle stopped on the carriageway with the triangular danger sign when it cannot be clearly seen from 100 metres away.
12w6w9b.why: Outside built-up areas the triangle is mandatory even by day if the vehicle cannot be clearly seen from 100 metres.

2wfawp.q: Outside built-up areas it is mandatory, even by day, to give advance warning of a load accidentally fallen onto the carriageway with the mobile triangular danger sign, when the obstruction cannot be clearly seen from 100 metres away.
2wfawp.why: Even by day, a fallen load must be marked with the triangle if it cannot be clearly seen from 100 metres.

iod4am.q: The mobile triangular danger sign is part of the compulsory equipment of motor vehicles.
iod4am.why: The warning triangle (segnale mobile triangolare di pericolo) is compulsory equipment on motor vehicles.

1uqi60p.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed behind the vehicle or obstacle to be marked, at least 50 metres away.
1uqi60p.why: The triangle must be placed behind the vehicle or obstacle, at least 50 metres away.

1drbyep.q: If there is an intersection less than 50 metres away, the mobile triangular danger sign must be placed behind the vehicle in the position best suited to being seen.
1drbyep.why: If an intersection is closer than 50 metres, the triangle goes in the position where it is most easily seen.

1tqvypb.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed on the carriageway so that it is visible from at least 100 metres by approaching vehicles.
1tqvypb.why: The triangle must be visible to approaching vehicles from at least 100 metres.

1aiz0ho.q: Outside built-up areas, at night, when the rear position or emergency lights are missing or insufficient, it is advisable to give advance warning of a vehicle stopped on the carriageway with the mobile triangular danger sign.
1aiz0ho.why: In this situation warning with the triangle is not merely advisable; it is mandatory.

pr9ume.q: The mobile danger triangle must be used compulsorily to mark a vehicle stopped by breakdown at night if the obstacle is not visible from at least 150 metres away.
pr9ume.why: The visibility threshold is 100 metres, not 150.

velclu.q: Outside built-up areas, it is optional to give advance warning, even by day, of a load accidentally fallen on the carriageway with the danger sign, when it cannot be clearly seen from 100 metres away.
velclu.why: In that situation the triangle is mandatory, not optional.

11566fv.q: At night, when the rear position or emergency lights are missing or insufficient, it is mandatory to give advance warning of a stopped vehicle with the mobile triangular danger sign even inside built-up areas.
11566fv.why: Inside built-up areas there is no such obligation; it applies outside built-up areas.

1j2dh7t.q: At night, when the rear position lights are missing or insufficient, it is mandatory to give advance warning of stopped bicycles, mopeds and motorcycles with the mobile triangular danger sign, even inside built-up areas.
1j2dh7t.why: The obligation does not apply inside built-up areas, and the triangle is not required for bicycles, mopeds and motorcycles.

1wcl8ik.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed on the load that has accidentally fallen onto the carriageway.
1wcl8ik.why: The triangle goes at a distance (at least 50 metres) behind the load, not on it.

148nyix.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed on the carriageway so that it is visible from a distance of at least 50 metres by approaching vehicles.
148nyix.why: The required visibility is at least 100 metres, not 50.

1k1ngyt.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed in the lane occupied by the stopped vehicle or the fallen load.
1k1ngyt.why: The triangle is placed in the lane occupied by the stopped vehicle or fallen load.

2xm7or.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed on the carriageway at least one metre from its outer edge.
2xm7or.why: The triangle must be at least one metre from the outer edge of the carriageway.

1j7sn29.q: On a multi-lane carriageway, the mobile triangular danger sign must be placed in the lane immediately to the left of the stopped vehicle or fallen load.
1j7sn29.why: The triangle goes in the lane occupied by the vehicle or load, not in the lane to its left.

x1a4ot.q: The mobile triangular danger sign must be placed on the carriageway at least one metre from the dividing line between the directions of travel.
x1a4ot.why: The one-metre minimum is measured from the outer edge of the carriageway, not from the line separating the directions of travel.

16ac4i0.q: During advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign, the driver must make himself visible by wearing the high-visibility reflective jacket or braces.
16ac4i0.why: While placing the triangle the driver must wear a high-visibility reflective jacket or braces (giubbotto o bretelle retroriflettenti).

n6edmo.q: The high-visibility reflective jacket or braces to be used during advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign must be of an approved type.
n6edmo.why: The jacket or braces must be of an approved type (tipo approvato).

67bjwf.q: During advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign, the driver must wear the high-visibility jacket even when on emergency lanes or in lay-bys.
67bjwf.why: The obligation also applies on emergency lanes (corsie di emergenza) and rest areas (piazzole di sosta).

nth342.q: To carry out advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign, the driver is forbidden to get out of the vehicle and walk on the road without wearing the high-visibility jacket.
nth342.why: The driver may not leave the vehicle and walk on the road to place the triangle without the high-visibility jacket.

c4qyfv.q: During advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign, the use of the high-visibility reflective jacket or braces is optional.
c4qyfv.why: Wearing the high-visibility jacket or braces is compulsory, not optional.

1vrejlp.q: During advance-warning operations with the mobile danger sign, the driver must not wear the high-visibility jacket if he is on emergency lanes or in lay-bys.
1vrejlp.why: The jacket must be worn on emergency lanes and lay-bys too.

nk7kep.q: The driver must wear the high-visibility jacket at night, even inside built-up areas, if he has to stop on the carriageway because his vehicle has a fault.
nk7kep.why: The jacket obligation applies outside built-up areas, when getting out to place the triangle; it is not required inside built-up areas.

2u7f0z.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, cars that cannot, by construction, reach a level-ground speed of at least 80 km/h are forbidden.
2u7f0z.why: Cars that by design cannot reach 80 km/h on level ground are banned.

1bywzyk.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, agricultural machines are forbidden.
1bywzyk.why: Agricultural machinery (macchine agricole) may not use motorways or main extra-urban roads.

gf8dpe.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, vehicles with a disorderly, insecurely fastened load or a load projecting beyond permitted limits are forbidden.
gf8dpe.why: Vehicles with an untidy, unsecured or overhanging load beyond the limits are banned.

mpa6n1.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, vehicles that are not watertight and carry an uncovered load of materials that can scatter are forbidden.
mpa6n1.why: Non-watertight vehicles with an uncovered load of materials that can scatter are banned.

1jhmzwe.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, vehicles whose condition of use, equipment and tyres may endanger traffic are forbidden.
1jhmzwe.why: Vehicles whose condition, equipment or tyres may be dangerous are banned.

1qbq0zv.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, buses carrying students are forbidden.
1qbq0zv.why: Buses, including those carrying students, are allowed on these roads.

1eghzvk.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, it is advisable to avoid vehicles that are not watertight and carry an uncovered load of materials that can scatter.
1eghzvk.why: It is not merely advice: these vehicles are prohibited.

a670xv.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, vehicles carrying live animals are forbidden.
a670xv.why: Vehicles carrying live animals are allowed on these roads.

c8g609.q: Mopeds that reach a speed of at least 50 km/h are allowed on motorways and main extra-urban roads.
c8g609.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are not allowed on these roads, whatever their speed.

1mnmdfj.q: Agricultural machines not towing a trailer are allowed on motorways and main extra-urban roads.
1mnmdfj.why: Agricultural machines are banned, with or without a trailer.

137dr5z.q: Vehicles without tyres, if secured, are allowed on motorways and main extra-urban roads.
137dr5z.why: Vehicles without tyres (pneumatici) may not use these roads.

f1mas9.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, pedestrians and animals are forbidden, except in service areas and rest areas.
f1mas9.why: Pedestrians and animals are banned, except in service areas (aree di servizio) and rest areas (aree di sosta).

1gncmfe.q: In service areas and rest areas of motorways and main extra-urban roads, animals may move about only if properly supervised.
1gncmfe.why: In service and rest areas animals may move around only if properly supervised.

1e9klzu.q: On motorway emergency lanes, pedestrians may walk only to reach the emergency call points.
1e9klzu.why: On emergency lanes pedestrians may walk only to reach the emergency call points (punti per le richieste di soccorso).

fkbolj.q: On motorways, towing of broken-down vehicles on carriageways, ramps, junctions, service or parking areas is allowed only to authorised rescue vehicles.
fkbolj.why: On motorways only authorised rescue vehicles may tow a broken-down vehicle.

q8ptsc.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, pedestrians and animals are forbidden, even in service areas and rest areas.
q8ptsc.why: The ban has an exception: pedestrians and animals are allowed in service and rest areas.

zq32qv.q: In service areas and rest areas of motorways and main extra-urban roads, animals may not move about even if properly supervised.
zq32qv.why: Animals may move around in service and rest areas if properly supervised.

dblp50.q: On carriageways, ramps, junctions, service or parking areas and any other motorway appurtenance, asking for or giving lifts is forbidden.
dblp50.why: Asking for or offering lifts is banned on the whole motorway and its appurtenances (pertinenze).

qvp3uq.q: In motorway service or parking areas and any other motorway appurtenance, commercial activities may be carried out only if authorised by the road owner.
qvp3uq.why: Commercial activities need authorisation from the road owner (ente proprietario).

78ue.q: On carriageways, ramps, junctions, service or parking areas and any other motorway appurtenance, camping is allowed only in areas set aside for it and for the period set by the road owner.
78ue.why: Camping is allowed only in designated areas and for the period set by the road owner.

oy99kn.q: In motorway service areas, the driver must not leave the vehicle parked for more than 24 hours.
oy99kn.why: In service areas parking must not exceed 24 hours.

cnfcgf.q: On motorways it is permitted to give lifts to disabled people.
cnfcgf.why: Giving lifts on motorways is banned for everyone, with no exceptions.

180oi6f.q: In motorway service areas or parking areas it is permitted to ask for and give lifts.
180oi6f.why: The ban on asking for or giving lifts also applies in service and parking areas.

6am2sj.q: In service or parking areas of motorways and main extra-urban roads, camping is permitted.
6am2sj.why: Camping is allowed only in designated areas and for the period set by the road owner.

mdu8z9.q: In motorway service and parking areas, the maximum parking time for a vehicle is three hours.
mdu8z9.why: The maximum stay in service areas is 24 hours, not three.

1g5qdl8.q: While driving on motorways and main extra-urban roads, use of dipped headlights is compulsory even by day.
1g5qdl8.why: On motorways and main extra-urban roads dipped headlights (anabbaglianti) are compulsory even by day.

1tek5ip.q: While driving on motorways and main extra-urban roads, use of dipped headlights is optional in perfect visibility.
1tek5ip.why: Dipped headlights are always compulsory, even in perfect visibility.

1p5ve9w.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, it is forbidden to reverse direction and to cross the central reservation, even at the gaps.
1p5ve9w.why: U-turns and crossing the central reservation (spartitraffico) are banned, even at gaps (varchi).

q8izd.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, it is forbidden to drive on the carriageway or part of it in the direction opposite to the permitted one.
q8izd.why: Driving the wrong way on any part of the carriageway is banned.

v9r8w4.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, reversing is forbidden.
v9r8w4.why: Reversing (retromarcia) is banned on carriageways, ramps and junctions.

12ewj03.q: On motorway emergency stopping lanes, reversing is forbidden.
12ewj03.why: Reversing is banned on emergency lanes too.

1od49oq.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, the driver may reverse direction by taking all necessary precautions.
1od49oq.why: U-turns are always banned, whatever precautions are taken.

15acohe.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, the driver may reverse direction in cases of particular emergency.
15acohe.why: U-turns are banned even in an emergency.

ygirln.q: On carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways and main extra-urban roads, the driver may proceed against the normal flow of traffic for short stretches.
ygirln.why: Driving against the traffic flow is banned even for short stretches.

y30qix.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, the driver may use the emergency lane if traffic is heavy.
y30qix.why: The emergency lane is reserved for emergency stops and rescue vehicles, even in heavy traffic.

1mg4n5i.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, a driver on the acceleration lane must give way to vehicles travelling in the running lanes.
1mg4n5i.why: A driver on the acceleration lane (corsia di accelerazione) must give way to vehicles on the through lanes.

n9d9cw.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, to leave the carriageway the driver must move into the right-hand lane in good time and then enter the deceleration lane from its start.
n9d9cw.why: To exit, get into the right lane early and enter the deceleration lane (corsia di decelerazione) at its start.

fiu44b.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, the driver must signal a lane change in good time using the direction indicators.
fiu44b.why: Lane changes must always be signalled in good time with the indicators, especially where speeds are high.

kuojy8.q: In a traffic jam on main extra-urban roads or motorways, if the emergency lane is missing or not usable by police or rescue vehicles, the driver in the right-hand lane must keep as close as possible to the left line.
kuojy8.why: Without a usable emergency lane, the driver in the rightmost lane moves as far left as possible to leave room for emergency vehicles.

1ls4dcv.q: In a traffic jam, the driver may use the emergency stopping lane only to leave the motorway, starting from the advance exit sign placed 500 metres from the interchange.
1ls4dcv.why: In a jam the emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) may be used only to exit, from the advance exit sign 500 metres before the junction.

15pn4jt.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, to leave the carriageway the driver may enter the deceleration lane even in the part after its start.
15pn4jt.why: The deceleration lane (corsia di decelerazione) must be entered right at its beginning, not further along.

1d7kk5c.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, if traffic is light the driver is not obliged to use the direction indicators to signal a lane change.
1d7kk5c.why: The duty to signal a lane change with the indicators always applies, even when traffic is light.

7r42d0.q: On motorways and main extra-urban roads, driving in parallel lines is allowed even when there is no traffic.
7r42d0.why: Driving in parallel lines is allowed only in heavy traffic; otherwise vehicles must keep to the rightmost free lane.

5xa33d.q: On the carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways, stopping is allowed only in emergencies caused by illness of the driver or passengers or by a vehicle fault.
5xa33d.why: On motorways you may stop only in an emergency: illness of the driver or passengers, or a vehicle breakdown.

17u2awf.q: On the carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways, if a passenger feels unwell it is permitted to stop in the emergency stopping lane.
17u2awf.why: A passenger's illness counts as an emergency, so stopping in the emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is allowed.

1x8c5sc.q: On the carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways, an emergency stop must not exceed the time strictly necessary and in any case must not last beyond three hours.
1x8c5sc.why: An emergency stop must last only as long as strictly necessary and never more than three hours.

1jy4jnm.q: If a passenger feels unwell while travelling on a motorway carriageway, it is permitted to stop in the emergency stopping lane.
1jy4jnm.why: A passenger's illness justifies stopping in the emergency lane (corsia di emergenza).

okcsby.q: On the carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways, it is forbidden to park or stop if passengers feel unwell.
okcsby.why: Passenger illness is one of the emergencies that allow you to stop in the emergency lane.

z8s7bh.q: On the carriageways, ramps and junctions of motorways, an emergency stop must not exceed the time strictly necessary and may last up to 24 hours.
z8s7bh.why: An emergency stop may never last more than three hours, not 24.

17l7u3.q: On a motorway it is forbidden to give a lift to a motorist stopped in the emergency lane because of a vehicle breakdown.
17l7u3.why: Stopping to give lifts on a motorway is forbidden; a driver with a breakdown must wait for assistance.

1w75e4w.q: If a driver sees a motorist stopped with a broken-down vehicle on the motorway, they must escort them to the nearest service area.
1w75e4w.why: You may not stop or escort anyone; the stranded driver should call for help via the SOS phones or emergency numbers.

d2t00u.q: If a driver sees a motorist stopped on the motorway with a broken-down vehicle, they must stop to help.
d2t00u.why: Stopping to help is forbidden on a motorway; you may instead alert the emergency services.

1qjp2u1.q: If a driver sees a motorist stopped on the motorway with a broken-down vehicle and has already passed them, they may carefully reverse to help.
1qjp2u1.why: Reversing (retromarcia) is always forbidden on a motorway, even to help someone.

ekcj6s.q: If a driver sees a motorist stopped on the motorway with a broken-down vehicle, they may carefully tow it to the first exit toll booth.
ekcj6s.why: On a motorway a passing driver may not tow a broken-down vehicle; the stranded driver must call a recovery service.

5qmzp1.q: All passengers in motor vehicles must take their seats so as not to limit the driver's freedom of movement or obstruct visibility.
5qmzp1.why: Passengers must sit so that they do not restrict the driver's movement or view.

1v29jw.q: The maximum number of seats in cars is stated on the vehicle registration document.
1v29jw.why: The maximum number of seats is stated on the registration document (carta di circolazione).

ersb46.q: Carrying one pet animal in vehicles is permitted, provided it does not hinder or endanger driving.
ersb46.why: One pet may be carried as long as it does not obstruct or endanger the driver.

fwizx3.q: Carrying more than one pet in vehicles is permitted, provided they are kept in a cage or in the rear compartment separated by a net.
fwizx3.why: Several pets may be carried if they are in a cage or in the rear space divided off by a net.

rph9s6.q: The number of people that can be carried in cars, as shown on the registration document, does not include the driver.
rph9s6.why: The number of persons on the registration document (carta di circolazione) includes the driver.

u5xgun.q: The number of people that can be carried in cars may reach a maximum of ten.
u5xgun.why: A car may carry at most nine people, driver included.

13ys2ap.q: Carrying dogs in vehicles, even more than one, is permitted provided they are properly held on a leash.
13ys2ap.why: Several animals need a cage or a netted rear compartment; a leash alone is not enough.

155wlvj.q: Carrying children under 5 years of age on motorcycles is forbidden.
155wlvj.why: Children under five may not be carried on motorcycles.

19bi7el.q: Motorcycle riders are forbidden to tow or be towed by other vehicles.
19bi7el.why: Motorcyclists may neither tow other vehicles nor be towed.

c98acj.q: On motorcycles it is forbidden to carry objects that are not firmly secured.
c98acj.why: Loads on motorcycles must be firmly secured so they cannot fall or affect riding.

qrlkec.q: On motorcycles it is forbidden to carry objects that prevent or limit the rider's visibility.
qrlkec.why: The load must not reduce the rider's visibility.

12awm1r.q: On motorcycles it is possible to carry a passenger only if the passenger is of legal age.
12awm1r.why: The passenger may be a minor, as long as he or she is at least five years old.

1nx1brx.q: Motorcycles are allowed to be towed, but only by cars.
1nx1brx.why: Motorcycles may not be towed by any vehicle.

51uauh.q: On motorcycles it is forbidden to carry objects that project longitudinally beyond the outline of the vehicle.
51uauh.why: Limited longitudinal overhang is permitted on motorcycles within set limits, so it is not absolutely forbidden.

um6e3j.q: The load of vehicles must be arranged so as to prevent it from falling or scattering.
um6e3j.why: Loads must be placed so that they cannot fall or scatter.

118ezr9.q: The load of vehicles must be arranged so as not to reduce the driver's visibility or restrict freedom of movement while driving.
118ezr9.why: The load must not limit the driver's view or freedom of movement.

1pntmdr.q: The load of vehicles must be arranged so as not to compromise the stability of the vehicle.
1pntmdr.why: The load must be arranged so that it does not affect the vehicle's stability.

qvqynl.q: The load of vehicles must be arranged so as not to hide lighting and visual signalling devices, number plates or arm signals.
qvqynl.why: The load must not cover lights, signalling devices, number plates or hand signals.

1fj5mcc.q: The vehicle's load must be arranged to prevent it from falling or scattering only if the driver is going to drive on an extra-urban road.
1fj5mcc.why: Loads must always be secured, on any type of road.

9d8nri.q: The load of vehicles must be arranged so as not to hide lighting and visual signalling devices only during night-time driving.
9d8nri.why: The load must never cover lights and signals, by day or by night.

1m7laco.q: The load must not exceed the maximum outline limit set for each type of vehicle.
1m7laco.why: The load may not exceed the maximum dimensions (sagoma) set for each vehicle type.

vagto4.q: On motor vehicles, the load may not project longitudinally from the front.
vagto4.why: No load overhang is allowed at the front.

11llvog.q: The load may project longitudinally from the rear, if made up of indivisible items, up to 3/10 of the length of the motor vehicle.
11llvog.why: At the rear, indivisible loads may overhang by up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length.

1oxvj5g.q: On motor vehicles, items may be carried that project sideways beyond the vehicle outline by no more than 30 centimetres from the front and rear position lights (always within the maximum outline limits).
1oxvj5g.why: Sideways overhang is limited to 30 cm from the position lights, within the maximum width limits.

1yf51e9.q: It is forbidden to carry or tow things that drag along the ground, even if partly supported by wheels.
1yf51e9.why: Carrying or towing things that drag on the ground is forbidden, even if partly supported by wheels.

1nqo6xq.q: If the load projects beyond the vehicle's outline, the driver must take all suitable precautions to avoid danger to other road users.
1nqo6xq.why: With an overhanging load the driver must take every suitable precaution to avoid endangering others.

1im9u1p.q: The load must be placed on the vehicle so as to signal its rear overhang with the retroreflective panel shown.
1im9u1p.why: The striped yellow-red panel shown marks heavy vehicles; rear overhang is marked by the square red-and-white panel.

1tvwb6x.q: The load may project sideways, if made up of indivisible items, up to 3/10 of the vehicle's width.
1tvwb6x.why: Sideways overhang is limited to 30 cm from the position lights, not 3/10 of the width.

1oz8tne.q: It is permitted to carry or tow things that drag along the ground if partly supported by wheels.
1oz8tne.why: Carrying or towing things that drag on the ground is forbidden, even when partly supported by wheels.

l55bdj.q: The longitudinal overhang of the load, up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length, must be signalled by one or two square panels shown in the figure.
l55bdj.why: The square red-and-white striped panel, one or two of them, marks a load overhanging at the rear.

1k2yea.q: The panel shown must be applied in every case where the load projects at the rear, even slightly.
1k2yea.why: The square red-and-white panel is required for any rear overhang, however slight.

17qpmhl.q: The panel shown signals indivisible loads projecting from the rear of the vehicle.
17qpmhl.why: The square red-and-white striped panel marks indivisible loads that project from the rear.

jloih9.q: If the load projects longitudinally across the whole width of the rear of the vehicle, the panels shown must be two, placed crosswise at the two ends of the load.
jloih9.why: If the overhang spans the full width, two panels are used, placed crosswise at the ends of the load.

51dwk1.q: The longitudinal overhang of the load, up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length, must be signalled by one or two of the panels shown.
51dwk1.why: The striped yellow-red panel is for heavy vehicles; overhang is marked by the square red-and-white panel.

1nwuuld.q: The panel shown signals indivisible loads that project from the rear right-hand side.
1nwuuld.why: This chevron panel with a mandatory arrow marks an obstacle to be passed on the right, not a projecting load.

ntx1z7.q: If the load projects longitudinally across the whole width of the rear of the vehicle, two of the retroreflective panels shown must be applied.
ntx1z7.why: The yellow panel with red border marks lorry-trailer combinations; projecting loads need the red-and-white panel.

lq3qz9.q: The orange retroreflective panel shown signals vehicles that are carrying dangerous goods.
lq3qz9.why: The orange panel with identification numbers marks vehicles carrying dangerous goods.

19byl97.q: The panel shown makes it easier to identify, from behind, lorries with a laden mass above 3.5 tonnes.
19byl97.why: The yellow-and-red striped panel goes on the rear of lorries over 3.5 t laden mass.

1mluhqw.q: The yellow panel shown, placed on the rear of the trailer, identifies a road train or an articulated lorry.
1mluhqw.why: The yellow panel with red border on the rear of the trailer identifies a lorry-trailer combination (autotreno or autoarticolato).

n4fxmp.q: The orange retroreflective panel shown is placed at the rear to signal dangerous projecting loads.
n4fxmp.why: The orange panel with numbers indicates dangerous goods, not projecting loads.

lc2e5k.q: The panels shown are placed on the carriageway to signal an obstacle.
lc2e5k.why: The yellow-and-red striped panels are fitted on the rear of heavy vehicles, not placed on the carriageway.

1it4nww.q: The panel shown must be applied to the rear of buses with a total mass above 3.5 tonnes.
1it4nww.why: The yellow panel with red border goes on trailers of lorry combinations, not on buses.

1qftsrd.q: No vehicle may tow or be towed by more than one vehicle (except for exceptional transports).
1qftsrd.why: A vehicle may not tow or be towed by more than one vehicle, except for exceptional transports.

2hpv9l.q: A motor vehicle may tow a vehicle that is not a trailer if the latter can no longer travel because of a breakdown or lack of essential parts.
2hpv9l.why: A vehicle that cannot move because of a breakdown or missing essential parts may be towed.

abelkh.q: Emergency towing of one vehicle by another must be done through a solid connection, such as a rope, chain, cable or rigid bar, provided it is suitably signalled.
abelkh.why: Emergency towing needs a solid connection, suitably signalled.

suxyzg.q: Towing a broken-down vehicle in an urgent emergency must be done through a solid connection, provided it is suitably signalled so the vehicles are clearly visible to other road users.
suxyzg.why: The connection must be solid and signalled so that the vehicles are clearly visible to others.

1yi989h.q: If, in an emergency, a driver tows another vehicle without respecting the rules on the solidity of the connection, they are punished with the deduction of 2 points from the licence.
1yi989h.why: Towing in an emergency without a solid connection costs 2 licence points.

1awxd88.q: On a motorway, a motor vehicle may tow a vehicle that is not a trailer if the latter can no longer travel for any serious reason.
1awxd88.why: Towing a non-trailer vehicle on a motorway is forbidden, whatever the reason.

1op16w2.q: Towing a broken-down vehicle in an urgent emergency must be done through a solid connection, even if it is not possible to signal it.
1op16w2.why: If the tow cannot be signalled, it must not be carried out, even with a solid connection.

njfnf9.q: During towing of a broken-down vehicle, the towed vehicle must keep its rear lights on in the absence of other suitable signalling.
njfnf9.why: Without other suitable signalling, the towed vehicle needs more than just rear lights, namely its hazard and signalling lights.

js7f4j.q: If, in an emergency, a driver tows another vehicle without respecting the rules on the solidity of the connection, they are punished with the deduction of 4 points from the licence.
js7f4j.why: The penalty for a non-solid connection is 2 points off the licence, not 4.

cmm8je.q: The driver of a car must consider the risks on the road linked to the presence of bicycles, vehicles of modest mass characterised by low speeds and possible sideways swaying.
cmm8je.why: Bicycles are light, slow and may sway sideways, so drivers must allow for them.

ylcoro.q: The driver of a car or motorcycle must adapt their driving also to the risks linked to the presence of bicycles in traffic.
ylcoro.why: Car and motorcycle drivers must adjust their driving to the risks posed by cyclists.

1o1fgf8.q: The driver of a car must pay particular attention to bicycles ridden by very young, inexperienced riders or by elderly people.
1o1fgf8.why: Very young, inexperienced or elderly cyclists are less predictable and require extra care.

xhx06w.q: For a cyclist about to make a manoeuvre, it is very difficult to judge the approach speed of motor vehicles in traffic.
xhx06w.why: Cyclists find it hard to judge how fast motor vehicles are approaching.

9vxtqa.q: The driver of a car must anticipate the difficulty a cyclist, on the same lane and about to turn left, has in judging the speed of their vehicle.
9vxtqa.why: A cyclist turning left misjudges the speed of the vehicle behind, and the driver must anticipate this.

4rm4y8.q: The driver must show particular caution when driving near an elderly cyclist who, to check the road behind, turns the torso with difficulty and slowness because of advanced age.
4rm4y8.why: An elderly cyclist has difficulty checking behind, so extra caution is needed.

d300ib.q: The presence of children on bicycles in extra-urban traffic, even if riding side by side, is no risk to someone driving a motor vehicle, given their modest speed.
d300ib.why: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and vulnerable, and their low speed does not remove the risk.

35nps6.q: Cyclists can travel in complete safety in extra-urban traffic because motor vehicle drivers are always able to foresee their possible falls or dangerous swerves caused by an uneven road surface.
35nps6.why: Cyclists' falls and swerves are unpredictable, so they are never completely safe.

e5oiax.q: The approach speed of a car, especially on extra-urban roads, is easily judged from a distance by a cyclist riding slowly.
e5oiax.why: A cyclist finds it hard to judge the speed of an approaching car, especially outside towns.

b8h6yg.q: The driver of a car must constantly remember the risk posed by moped riders with limited driving experience because of their young age.
b8h6yg.why: Young moped (ciclomotore) riders have little experience, so drivers must always bear this in mind.

138pcm5.q: The left turn is particularly dangerous for a moped, which must cross the path of one or more columns of faster vehicles coming in the same direction.
138pcm5.why: A left turn forces a moped to cross the path of faster vehicles behind, which is very dangerous.

nlnv5o.q: The driver of a motor vehicle must carefully assess, in relation to their own speed, the distance separating them from a moped rider about to turn.
nlnv5o.why: The driver must carefully judge the gap to a turning moped rider in relation to his own speed.

yh6bgm.q: The driver of a motor vehicle must anticipate sudden manoeuvres by others, such as a moped weaving in a zig-zag.
yh6bgm.why: Drivers must anticipate other road users' sudden manoeuvres, such as a moped zig-zagging.

jo10ks.q: The driver of a motor vehicle or motorcycle must keep a safe lateral distance from cyclists or moped riders so as not to endanger their balance.
jo10ks.why: A safe side gap avoids upsetting the balance of cyclists and moped riders.

tdm3tp.q: The driver of a motor vehicle must avoid sideways deviations, even slight ones, especially near moped riders or cyclists, to prevent them from falling.
tdm3tp.why: Even slight sideways deviations can make cyclists and moped riders fall, so they must be avoided.

dyjya8.q: The driver of a motor vehicle must comply with traffic rules, but is not required to anticipate the possible carelessness of a moped rider travelling alongside.
dyjya8.why: A driver must obey the rules and also anticipate other road users' possible mistakes, especially those of vulnerable riders such as moped users.

1kd23vu.q: It is easy for a car driver to judge the distance from a moped rider who brakes suddenly to turn into a poorly signposted road.
1kd23vu.why: Judging the distance to a moped that suddenly slows to turn into a poorly signposted road is difficult, so extra caution is needed.

13paj8y.q: A car driver may overtake a moped rider at high speed, within the limits, despite the small lateral safety distance.
13paj8y.why: Overtaking fast with little side clearance is dangerous even within the speed limit. Leave enough lateral space and reduce speed.

1d3ae0d.q: A car driver must know the risks posed by particularly slow vehicles, such as three-wheeled mopeds, especially on extra-urban roads.
1d3ae0d.why: On extra-urban roads very slow vehicles such as three-wheeled mopeds are a hazard that the driver must know about and anticipate.

1b0wi6i.q: For a car travelling fast, within the limits, on a two-lane extra-urban road, a three-wheeled moped is a potential hazard, especially if it makes sudden manoeuvres.
1b0wi6i.why: The big speed difference makes a three-wheeled moped a potential hazard, especially if it manoeuvres suddenly.

1ngzf5n.q: For a car driver travelling at a regular speed on an extra-urban road, it can be hard to judge the speed of an agricultural machine, which usually moves slowly.
1ngzf5n.why: A very slow vehicle such as farm machinery is hard to judge, in speed and distance, for a driver approaching faster, so extra attention is needed.

yvxdmi.q: The presence of vehicles that can reach very different speeds, especially on extra-urban roads, is a safety factor.
yvxdmi.why: Big speed differences between vehicles increase the risk of accidents; they are not a safety factor.

cqlesk.q: It is easy to judge the time needed to close in on a slow vehicle for a car travelling fast, within the limits, especially on an extra-urban road.
cqlesk.why: When approaching a slow vehicle at speed, estimating time and distance is difficult, so you risk arriving too close.

1mwrci6.q: A collision between vehicles with very different masses is particularly dangerous.
1mwrci6.why: When masses differ greatly, the lighter vehicle suffers the worst consequences of the impact.

1wl25mz.q: When driving a small car, you must consider the greater risks of rear-end or other collisions with a heavier car.
1wl25mz.why: In a crash with a heavier vehicle, the small car suffers more damage, so this risk must be taken into account.

igd7xc.q: A car with a large mass offers, in traffic, a guarantee of safety also for other vehicles of smaller size and mass.
igd7xc.why: A large mass does not protect others: in a crash smaller, lighter vehicles are the ones that suffer most.

14lhejq.q: Vehicles are safer in traffic the more their masses differ.
14lhejq.why: Very different masses make collisions more dangerous, so they do not make traffic safer.

j5kfl0.q: Large differences in performance and mass between cars make for good road safety.
j5kfl0.why: Large differences in performance and mass increase risks in traffic and worsen road safety.

xgpbk1.q: The driver of an off-road vehicle (SUV) must drive with maximum caution, aware that the vehicle's height and mass are a potential danger to pedestrians, cyclists and small cars.
xgpbk1.why: A SUV's height and mass are a potential danger to pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, so maximum caution is needed.

16g3wka.q: Drivers of off-road vehicles (SUVs) must consider the serious damage that their vehicle's protruding, reinforced bumpers can cause in an impact with smaller vehicles.
16g3wka.why: Protruding, reinforced bumpers on off-road vehicles can cause serious damage to smaller vehicles in an impact.

1pix28h.q: The driver of an off-road vehicle (SUV) must remember that driving it is particularly demanding in town and requires special care, above all in emergency manoeuvres.
1pix28h.why: An off-road vehicle is demanding in town because of its size and mass, and needs special care in emergency manoeuvres.

hrrhhq.q: Driving an off-road vehicle (SUV), with a large mass and a height greater than cars, guarantees maximum safety for its occupants and for other road users.
hrrhhq.why: Mass and height do not guarantee maximum safety, and for other road users an off-road vehicle is actually more dangerous.

u71s5c.q: In a collision or rear-end crash, protruding, reinforced bumpers (bull bars) make off-road vehicles less dangerous for other vehicles.
u71s5c.why: Reinforced, protruding bumpers (bull bars) make an off-road vehicle more dangerous, not less, for other vehicles.

3w2khu.q: Driving an off-road vehicle (SUV) is particularly suitable inside built-up areas.
3w2khu.why: An off-road vehicle is bulky and not well suited to town driving, where it demands particular caution.

w9qv01.q: When driving a car, it is advisable to constantly assess the potential danger of industrial vehicles and buses, because of their much greater mass.
w9qv01.why: Industrial vehicles and buses have much greater mass, so they are potentially more dangerous in a collision.

tb701j.q: A motorcycle or car driver must be able to assess the high risks arising from lorries, lorry-trailer combinations or articulated lorries that do not respect the speed limits.
tb701j.why: Heavy vehicles that exceed speed limits are very dangerous because of their mass, and other drivers must be able to assess this.

unpykb.q: Because of their large mass, lorries, lorry-trailer combinations and articulated lorries do not pose greater potential risks to a car or motorcycle than any other vehicle.
unpykb.why: Because of their large mass, these heavy vehicles pose a greater potential risk to cars and motorcycles.

1yoim3f.q: Even if the vehicle's construction allows an adequate field of view, while driving the driver must carefully observe the area ahead and around.
1yoim3f.why: Even with good built-in visibility, the driver must watch carefully the area ahead of and around the vehicle.

9hq4bx.q: A driver's field of view can be reduced both by a headrest and by parts of the car body, which may accidentally hide other road users.
9hq4bx.why: Headrests and body pillars can create blind spots and hide other road users.

1vrr140.q: To ensure adequate visibility, it is forbidden to apply adhesive films to the windscreen and front side windows of vehicles.
1vrr140.why: To ensure visibility, adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.

10vqtvw.q: Pedestrians, especially children, risk being outside the field of view of the driver of an off-road vehicle (SUV) because of the vehicle's size.
10vqtvw.why: Because of a SUV's size, pedestrians, especially children, can end up outside the driver's field of view.

1hs0d7e.q: The driver may limit himself to a hasty visual check of the area immediately in front of the vehicle, since the vehicle has an adequate field of view by construction.
1hs0d7e.why: Even with good visibility, the check of the area ahead must be careful, not hasty.

1gmp37l.q: It is permitted to apply adhesive films to the front side windows and windscreen, provided they are made of removable material.
1gmp37l.why: Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden, even if removable.

wzj62u.q: Off-road vehicles are tall enough to give the driver adequate visibility of all possible low obstacles (for example, children).
wzj62u.why: Despite their height, off-road vehicles have blind areas in front and close by where low obstacles, such as children, can be hidden.

13anc6q.q: Before moving off again, the driver of a lorry must pay particular attention to the possible presence of a pedestrian or cyclist in the area immediately in front of the stationary vehicle.
13anc6q.why: The area just in front of a lorry is hard to see from the cab, so before moving off the driver must watch closely for pedestrians and cyclists.

rjw46d.q: The driver of a lorry stopped at a traffic light must expect pedestrians and cyclists who cannot be seen because of the vehicle's shape.
rjw46d.why: The lorry's shape can hide nearby pedestrians and cyclists, and the driver must expect them to be there.

1rcfcyx.q: The limited view through a lorry's windscreen of the area immediately in front makes it dangerous for such vehicles to stop in a queue when pedestrians or two-wheelers are present.
1rcfcyx.why: There is a poorly visible area in front of a lorry, which makes queuing dangerous when pedestrians or two-wheelers are nearby.

fzancz.q: The field of view of lorries allows safe control of the whole area immediately in front and at the sides.
fzancz.why: Lorries have blind spots in front and at the sides, so the view of the area is not complete.

fv8tep.q: A pedestrian can safely cross the road passing very close to the front of a lorry standing in a queue that is about to move off, since the driver will surely see him.
fv8tep.why: There is an area in front of the lorry that the driver cannot see, so passing close to its front is very dangerous.

1kr3qgy.q: When about to move off after stopping at a traffic light, lorry drivers can easily see pedestrians or cyclists who stand beside and brush against the front of their vehicles.
1kr3qgy.why: Pedestrians and cyclists next to the front of a lorry are in a blind spot, and the driver cannot easily see them.

hqk23s.q: A high-visibility retroreflective vest or braces can in every case replace the portable warning triangle.
hqk23s.why: The vest makes you visible but does not replace the warning triangle, which is still required to signal a stopped vehicle.

1eplj0k.q: High-visibility retroreflective vests or braces may only be yellow.
1eplj0k.why: High-visibility vests or braces can come in different colours, such as yellow, orange or red, as long as they are retroreflective.

inncox.q: A retroreflective high-visibility vest also protects the driver from chemical hazards, heat, fire and electricity.
inncox.why: The vest only makes you visible by day and night; it offers no protection against chemicals, heat, fire or electricity.

1oz92i8.q: Inside the vehicle you must keep high-visibility retroreflective vests or braces, in a number equal to the available seats.
1oz92i8.why: You must carry at least one vest or pair of braces, not one for each seat.

1f4b33t.q: The obligation to wear the high-visibility vest applies when stopping outside built-up areas, while the retroreflective braces must be worn in urban areas.
1f4b33t.why: The vest and the braces are equivalent: wear one or the other when getting out of a stopped vehicle outside built-up areas.

1izpzex.q: The high-visibility retroreflective vest is used to ask passing motorists for help.
1izpzex.why: The vest makes the person who leaves the vehicle visible; it is not for asking passing drivers for help.

ve8fte.q: The high-visibility retroreflective vest is useful only when you have to change a punctured wheel.
ve8fte.why: The vest must be worn whenever you get out of a vehicle stopped on the carriageway outside built-up areas, not only to change a wheel.

xep45m.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load in danger of falling, it is advisable to increase the safety distance, especially uphill.
xep45m.why: Behind a load that may fall, increase the safety distance, especially uphill, to have more room to brake.

srgb0s.q: When driving behind a vehicle with an unstable load, it is advisable to increase the safety distance and overtake it as soon as possible.
srgb0s.why: Behind an unstable load, increase your distance and overtake as soon as possible, when conditions allow it.

70jrsi.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is advisable to warn the driver of the potential danger.
70jrsi.why: Warning the driver about the loose load, for example with light signals, is correct behaviour.

1jpwhzv.q: When driving behind a vehicle with an unsafe load, it is best not to stay too close, so as to be able to stop in time if the goods fall.
1jpwhzv.why: Staying well back lets you stop in time if the goods fall.

zrje3i.q: When driving behind a vehicle with an unstable load, you must be careful, especially when it brakes or turns, because the goods may fall.
zrje3i.why: Braking and turning are the moments when an unstable load can fall, so extra care is needed.

h5t2vs.q: When driving behind a vehicle with a protruding load, it may be hard to notice that it intends to turn if the turn indicators are hidden by the hanging goods.
h5t2vs.why: A protruding load can hide the turn indicators, making the manoeuvre hard to read.

1jqf3r3.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is best to keep as close as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.
1jqf3r3.why: Hugging the left edge is not helpful and is dangerous: increase your distance and stay in lane.

l2dy0i.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying an unsafe load, it is best to move along the left edge of the carriageway.
l2dy0i.why: Moving to the left is not helpful and can be dangerous; the right measure is to increase the safety distance.

ywjtwr.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is best to overtake it immediately, even on a bend.
ywjtwr.why: Overtaking on a bend is forbidden and dangerous; overtake only when it is safe and permitted.

cu6kx7.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is best to stop abruptly and set off again only after the other vehicles have passed.
cu6kx7.why: Braking abruptly is dangerous for those behind; increase your distance and brake gradually.

1kseh9s.q: When driving behind a vehicle carrying an unstable load, you must reduce the safety distance so that other vehicles give up overtaking, as there is not enough room.
1kseh9s.why: The safety distance must be increased, not reduced, so you can brake in time if the load falls.

1i06by9.q: Towing a trailer on roads with steep climbs raises the temperature of the engine coolant.
1i06by9.why: On steep climbs the engine works harder with a trailer, so the coolant temperature rises.

siwdu6.q: If you tow a trailer, the braking distance increases.
siwdu6.why: With a trailer the total mass is greater, so the braking distance increases.

rxqhnp.q: When towing a light trailer, you must consider that the overturning force exerted by the wind is greater.
rxqhnp.why: A light trailer is more affected by wind, which exerts a greater overturning force on it.

dkwj7i.q: For greater safety, it is advisable to arrange the load in the trailer so that heavy objects are as close as possible to its axle.
dkwj7i.why: Heavy objects should be placed close to the trailer's axle for better stability.

4td5w8.q: When driving a vehicle with a trailer and turning right, you must take particular care not to ride the rear wheel onto the pavement.
4td5w8.why: In right turns the trailer wheels track further inside and can climb onto the pavement.

oom0m1.q: When a broken-down vehicle fitted with power steering is towed, steering can be hard work.
oom0m1.why: With the engine off the power steering does not work, so steering takes much more effort.

16k7pxv.q: Before towing a trailer, it is advisable to make sure that the lighting and signalling systems work properly.
16k7pxv.why: The trailer must be visible and signal manoeuvres, so lights and signals must be checked beforehand.

1nzt0o1.q: Before starting to tow a trailer, you must check in the rear-view mirrors that visibility is adequate.
1nzt0o1.why: A trailer can reduce rear visibility, so check in the mirrors that you can see properly.

ir4v6j.q: When trailers are detached from the towing vehicle, they must have insurance cover that is also valid for static risk (when stationary).
ir4v6j.why: A trailer detached from the towing vehicle must have insurance that also covers static risk, meaning when stationary.

rs6uf0.q: Trailers towed by cars are generally fitted with an inertia brake.
rs6uf0.why: Light trailers towed by cars generally have an inertia brake, which works by the push on the tow hitch.

1cdjgqn.q: Trailers must have their own number plate.
1cdjgqn.why: Every trailer has its own number plate, separate from that of the towing vehicle.

1q6qtrl.q: To ensure greater safety when driving a vehicle with a trailer, it is advisable to concentrate the maximum load at the tow hitch.
1q6qtrl.why: The load should be distributed evenly, with heavy items near the axle, not concentrated at the tow hitch.

1wv6flv.q: To tow a trailer, it is not necessary to make the electrical connection between towing vehicle and trailer.
1wv6flv.why: The electrical connection is needed so the trailer's lights and signals work.

1gxtnvm.q: To drive a car towing a broken-down vehicle with a driver on board, a category E driving licence is required.
1gxtnvm.why: Towing a broken-down vehicle does not require a category E licence; the licence for the towing vehicle's category is enough.

1r356a3.q: The driver on board a broken-down vehicle being towed may be without a driving licence.
1r356a3.why: The person steering the towed vehicle must hold a licence valid for that vehicle.

t7a4cn.q: If a broken-down vehicle is towed with all four wheels on the ground, fourth gear must be engaged.
t7a4cn.why: The towed vehicle must be in neutral (folle), not in fourth gear.

193ym8u.q: The towing parts of a vehicle do not need to be lubricated periodically.
193ym8u.why: Towing components must be lubricated periodically so that they work well and safely.

1wwb098.q: The towing parts of a vehicle may be non-approved, provided trailers with a mass below 750 kilograms are towed.
1wwb098.why: Towing components must always be approved (omologati), whatever the trailer's mass.

1us32sf.q: If you tow a broken-down vehicle fitted with power steering, the steering will always be locked.
1us32sf.why: With power steering the wheel is not always locked; with the engine off it is just harder to turn.

fgw8g7.q: When towing a trailer on steep descents, you do not need to take into account the pushing force exerted by the trailer on the towing vehicle.
fgw8g7.why: On steep descents the trailer pushes the towing vehicle and this must be taken into account, for example by using engine braking.

dk9ch.q: To tow a light trailer, it is not necessary to make the electrical connection.
dk9ch.why: Even for a light trailer the electrical connection is required, for the lights and signals.

1m106a2.q: When towing a broken-down vehicle, the distance between the two vehicles must be at least 3 metres.
1m106a2.why: No minimum distance of 3 metres is required; the rope or bar connection must not exceed 5 metres.

87kgpn.q: When towing a trailer, you must consider that on tight bends the swept area is smaller.
87kgpn.why: On tight bends the trailer cuts the corner, so the swept width is greater, not smaller.

1wvexwl.q: The number of people that can be carried on vehicles is shown on the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione).
1wvexwl.why: The registration document (carta di circolazione) states the number of seats, and so how many people can be carried.

1a24k05.q: The maximum number of seats in cars is nine, including the driver's.
1a24k05.why: Cars have at most nine seats, the driver's included.

1q7suxc.q: The number of people that can be carried in cars is at most nine, including the driver.
1q7suxc.why: A car can carry at most nine people, driver included.

cnpzsu.q: The number of seats of a vehicle is shown on the registration document (carta di circolazione).
cnpzsu.why: The number of seats is stated on the registration document (carta di circolazione).

1qm3pql.q: The number of people that can be carried on motorcycles is always two in addition to the rider.
1qm3pql.why: On motorcycles one passenger may be carried only if the bike is approved for it; it is never always two.

177a6cd.q: The number of people that can be carried in cars is at most four.
177a6cd.why: Cars can have up to nine seats, driver included, not just four.

a0t1zm.q: The number of people that can be carried on lorries is always five, including the driver.
a0t1zm.why: The number of people on lorries depends on the seats stated on the registration document, not always five.

11ccnwl.q: The number of people a vehicle may carry, shown on the registration document, does not include the driver.
11ccnwl.why: The seating capacity on the registration document (carta di circolazione) includes the driver.

f5iot0.q: The panel shown must be placed at the end of a load that projects beyond the rear of the vehicle.
f5iot0.why: The red and white retroreflective square panel marks a load that sticks out behind the vehicle. It goes at the end of the load.

1dnzczf.q: The panel shown signals loads that project from the rear of the vehicle.
1dnzczf.why: The red and white retroreflective square panel marks a load that sticks out behind the vehicle.

b71l03.q: The panel shown must be retroreflective.
b71l03.why: The overhanging-load panel must be retroreflective so it can be seen at night too.

1yx2bd2.q: The panel shown must be used whenever the load projects behind the vehicle, even slightly.
1yx2bd2.why: The panel is required for any rear overhang of a load, however small.

1pzs0ow.q: The panel shown may be placed on broken-down vehicles being towed when their hazard lights do not work.
1pzs0ow.why: On a towed broken-down vehicle whose hazard lights do not work, this panel can be used to warn following drivers.

i92wbv.q: The panel shown must be fitted at the end of the load projecting from the vehicle, so that it is always clearly visible.
i92wbv.why: The panel must be fixed at the far end of the projecting load, where it is always clearly visible.

1669m42.q: The panel shown invites drivers behind the vehicle it is fitted to to drive with particular caution.
1669m42.why: The panel warns following drivers to proceed with extra caution because of the projecting load.

10pale1.q: The panel shown is used only if the load projects by more than three tenths of the vehicle's length.
10pale1.why: The panel is needed for any rear overhang; three tenths of the vehicle length is the maximum permitted overhang, not the threshold for using it.

148e7vd.q: The panel shown must also be placed at the side when the load projects beyond the width of the vehicle.
148e7vd.why: This panel is for rear overhang only; it is not the signal for a load projecting sideways.

k82gup.q: The panel shown identifies trucks specialised in transporting building materials.
k82gup.why: The panel does not identify any type of truck; it marks a load projecting from the rear of a vehicle.

1ma6et9.q: The panel shown must be placed on vehicles carrying rubbish.
1ma6et9.why: The panel has nothing to do with carrying rubbish; it is only for loads that project from the rear.

6ywjo1.q: The panel shown must be placed on vehicles only if the load projects by at least 50 centimetres.
6ywjo1.why: The panel is required for any rear overhang, with no 50 cm minimum threshold.

wev6cg.q: The panel shown must be placed on the back of all trucks.
wev6cg.why: The panel is used only when a load projects from the rear, not on every truck.

xogv9z.q: The panel shown may be replaced by a red flag measuring 50x50 centimetres.
xogv9z.why: The retroreflective panel is required to mark an overhanging load; a red flag cannot replace it.

1kilkn.q: In caravans, to reduce the risk of rolling over in bends, heavy objects must be loaded so as to keep the centre of gravity as low as possible.
1kilkn.why: Loading heavy items low lowers the centre of gravity and reduces the risk of rolling over in bends.

1dmggbs.q: In caravans, to reduce the risk of rolling over in bends, the load must be arranged as evenly as possible between the right and left sides.
1dmggbs.why: A load balanced between left and right keeps the caravan stable in bends.

940xsr.q: A caravan is not considered a trailer because it can be used as living accommodation.
940xsr.why: A caravan is legally a trailer (rimorchio), even though it can serve as accommodation.

1z0qnot.q: It is possible to stay in caravans (roulottes) while the vehicle is moving, provided all passengers wear seat belts.
1z0qnot.why: Nobody may ride inside a caravan while it is being towed, whether or not seat belts are fastened.

1b8py8w.q: A trailer has a safety device that automatically applies the parking brake if it accidentally becomes uncoupled.
1b8py8w.why: If the trailer accidentally detaches, a safety device automatically applies its parking brake.

10bo9xl.q: On trailers with an inertia brake, after a long period of inactivity the brakes may have lost efficiency because of rust.
10bo9xl.why: After long inactivity, rust can reduce the efficiency of inertia brakes, so they should be checked.

vin2s0.q: When leaving a trailer parked, the parking brake lever must be applied and, on a sloping road, it is advisable to put wedges (chocks) under the wheels.
vin2s0.why: When parking, apply the parking brake, and on a slope add wheel chocks (cunei).

83eorc.q: Braking of a trailer with an inertia brake does not happen at the same moment as the towing vehicle's, because it only operates after the trailer has pushed on the towing vehicle.
83eorc.why: An inertia brake only works once the trailer pushes against the towing vehicle, so it does not brake simultaneously.

12cv0be.q: In a trailer with an inertia brake, the braking effect occurs when the trailer moves closer to the towing vehicle.
12cv0be.why: The inertia brake acts when the trailer moves toward the towing vehicle and compresses the actuating device.

1o41krr.q: When driving a vehicle with a trailer, during braking in a straight line, the load carried will tend to shift backwards.
1o41krr.why: Under braking, inertia pushes the load forward, not backward.

12qvii9.q: When driving a vehicle with a trailer, during sharp acceleration in a straight line, the load carried will tend to shift forwards.
12qvii9.why: Under acceleration, the load tends to shift backward, not forward.

5f740.q: In cars fitted with ABS it is not possible to hitch a trailer without a braking system.
5f740.why: ABS does not prevent towing an unbraked trailer, provided the mass and towing-ratio limits are respected.

xyazur.q: On trailers fitted with an inertia brake, the trailer brakes at the same time as the towing vehicle.
xyazur.why: An inertia brake only engages after the trailer pushes on the towing vehicle, so there is a slight delay.

dou82k.q: On trailers fitted with an inertia brake, the trailer brakes about one second before the towing vehicle.
dou82k.why: An inertia-braked trailer never brakes before the towing vehicle; it brakes after, when it pushes on it.

dxpt6y.q: In built-up areas, the driver must not leave a trailer parked unhitched from the towing vehicle, unless otherwise indicated.
dxpt6y.why: In built-up areas a trailer may not be left parked detached from its towing vehicle unless signs allow it.

zixyrz.q: While in circulation, trailers must be insured under the same policy as the towing vehicle.
zixyrz.why: The towing vehicle's liability policy also covers the trailer attached to it.

1x5kj9x.q: External mirrors mounted on the towing vehicle must not project more than 20 centimetres from the outline of the vehicle (towing vehicle or trailer), measured at the point of greatest width.
1x5kj9x.why: Exterior mirrors on the towing vehicle may stick out at most 20 cm beyond the widest point of the outline.

16yktrr.q: The towing ratio, within the technically permitted limit for the vehicle, must not exceed 1 for trailers with a service brake and a mass up to 3.5 tonnes.
16yktrr.why: For braked trailers up to 3.5 t, the towing ratio may not exceed 1.

1ed2yvg.q: The maximum towing ratio for a trailer without any braking device is 0.5.
1ed2yvg.why: For an unbraked trailer the maximum towing ratio is 0.5.

jgfoil.q: When the towbar is not being used because no trailer is being towed, the part projecting beyond the rear outline of the vehicle must be removed, dismounted or folded away.
jgfoil.why: With no trailer attached, the part of the tow hitch that sticks out behind the vehicle must be removed or folded away.

1s6cjuk.q: T.A.T.S. trailers are intended for transporting equipment that must not be the object of trade, but used only for leisure.
1s6cjuk.why: T.A.T.S. trailers carry tourist and sports equipment for leisure use, not goods for sale.

9vnhpp.q: Drivers of motor vehicles towing a trailer, when the gross mass of the combination exceeds 3.5 tonnes, are considered drunk if a blood alcohol level above zero grams per litre is found.
9vnhpp.why: For combinations over 3.5 t the limit is zero: any alcohol level above 0 g/l counts as a violation.

wx3gfh.q: On motorways with carriageways of three or more lanes, drivers of vehicle combinations longer than 7 metres in total are forbidden from using lanes other than the two nearest the right edge of the carriageway.
wx3gfh.why: On motorways with three or more lanes, combinations over 7 m long may use only the two rightmost lanes.

12b1yfh.q: While in circulation, trailers with a maximum laden mass up to 3.5 tonnes must be marked with rear and side retroreflective strips.
12b1yfh.why: Rear and side retroreflective strips are required for trailers over 3.5 t, not for lighter ones.

1jhduiz.q: It is possible to tow unregistered trailers if their mass is below 750 kilograms.
1jhduiz.why: Every trailer, even a light one, must be registered to be used on the road.

1s045o.q: A trailer is considered an integral part of the vehicle if its mass is up to 3.5 tonnes.
1s045o.why: A trailer is a separate vehicle with its own plate and registration document, whatever its mass.

1j97tnr.q: The width of the trailer must not exceed that of the towing vehicle.
1j97tnr.why: A trailer may be wider than the towing vehicle as long as it stays within the legal maximum width.

u0li9d.q: The trailer is an integral part of the vehicle it was paired with during testing and cannot be hitched to another vehicle.
u0li9d.why: A trailer is not tied to one vehicle; it can be hitched to any other vehicle approved for towing it.

3v9h8j.q: When towing caravans and T.A.T.S. trailers, it is not compulsory for the towing vehicle to be fitted with a right-hand rear-view mirror.
3v9h8j.why: When towing a caravan or T.A.T.S. trailer, the towing vehicle must also have a right-hand mirror.

15wpf6o.q: External mirrors mounted on the towing vehicle may project up to 50 centimetres from the outline of the widest vehicle, if they are positioned at a height of no more than 1 metre from the ground.
15wpf6o.why: Mirrors may stick out at most 20 cm from the outline, with no exception based on height above the ground.

a82s5r.q: Within the maximum width set for T.A.T.S. trailers, transported boats may project up to 50 centimetres on each side beyond the outer edges of the rear position lights.
a82s5r.why: Sideways, a load may project at most 30 cm beyond the position lights, not 50.

1emic9x.q: The holder of a category BE driving licence who subsequently obtains a category C licence may also drive category CE vehicles.
1emic9x.why: Having BE and then getting C does not give CE; the CE licence must be obtained separately.

167a712.q: For vehicle combinations with trailers up to 3.5 tonnes of mass, there is no obligation to display at the rear the marks indicating their specific maximum speed limits.
167a712.why: The obligation to display the rear speed-limit marks also applies to combinations with trailers up to 3.5 t.

hx0qln.q: When towing a trailer carrying live animals, the hazard warning lights must be kept on to signal other drivers to increase their safety distance.
hx0qln.why: Hazard lights are not used to signal live-animal transport; they are only for danger or obstruction.

yan9fw.q: When towing a trailer, the towing vehicle's number plate must be removed and fixed to the rear of the trailer.
yan9fw.why: The trailer has its own plate and the towing vehicle keeps its own.

ek9fi5.q: If the registration document lacks the value of towable mass, this means the vehicle is suitable for towing trailers of any mass.
ek9fi5.why: If the towable mass is missing from the registration document, the vehicle is not approved for towing.

1l78d1s.q: Trailers must undergo periodic inspection together with the towing vehicle.
1l78d1s.why: Trailers have their own periodic inspection, with deadlines independent of the towing vehicle's.

f5if6t.q: On trailers, the load carried may project from the front up to 3/10 of the length of the vehicle combination.
f5if6t.why: No load may project at the front; only the rear may overhang, up to 3/10 of the length.

1pd7ldg.q: On light trailers, the load carried may project rearwards without any specific signalling obligation.
1pd7ldg.why: Even on light trailers, any rear overhang must be marked with the retroreflective panel.

u7pudx.q: Trailers for transporting horses (vans) cannot travel on motorways.
u7pudx.why: Horse trailers may use motorways, within the applicable speed limits.

bbb4s6.q: When driving a vehicle with a trailer, when turning right, particular care must be taken not to run over, with the right rear wheel, any pedestrians near the pavement.
bbb4s6.why: In right turns the trailer cuts the corner, so its rear wheel can hit pedestrians close to the kerb.

vy3onp.q: When towing a trailer, it must be remembered that in bends the space occupied is greater.
vy3onp.why: With a trailer, the combination sweeps a wider strip of road in bends.

sjihly.q: When towing a trailer on steep descents, the pushing force exerted by the trailer on the towing vehicle must be taken into account.
sjihly.why: On steep descents the trailer pushes on the towing vehicle and lengthens braking distances.

1ua3oq7.q: When towing a trailer, especially if loaded, there is a noticeable reduction in the vehicle's acceleration (pick-up).
1ua3oq7.why: The weight of a trailer, especially a loaded one, noticeably reduces the vehicle's pick-up.

1fg83x8.q: Before carrying out any manoeuvre with the trailer hitched, it is good practice to make sure there are no objects and/or people within the manoeuvring radius of the combination.
1fg83x8.why: Before manoeuvring with a trailer, check that no people or objects are in the combination's swing area.

rq6bfc.q: In bends the trailer tends to "cut in" because it follows a circular path with a smaller radius than the towing vehicle.
rq6bfc.why: The trailer follows a tighter radius than the towing vehicle, so it cuts the corner.

1k084t4.q: The movements of liquid inside a tank attached to a trailer during changes of direction, braking and acceleration are the main causes of instability in vehicle combinations.
1k084t4.why: Liquid sloshing in a tank during turns, braking and acceleration is a major cause of combination instability.

dcgj01.q: When towing a trailer, check that the load on the hitch does not alter the vehicle's attitude and the inclination of the headlight beam.
dcgj01.why: Hitch load can lower the rear and tilt the headlight beam up, dazzling oncoming drivers.

1s9ddlo.q: When going through a bend at moderate speed, the trailer always follows the same path as the towing vehicle.
1s9ddlo.why: A trailer never follows exactly the same path as the towing vehicle; it takes a tighter line in bends.

qhaor0.q: While driving, the trailer must have its manoeuvring jockey wheel (swivel wheel) lowered, resting on the ground.
qhaor0.why: The jockey wheel must be raised while driving, otherwise it would drag on the road.

1g0o4ll.q: In vehicles fitted with parking sensors, it is not possible to hitch a trailer.
1g0o4ll.why: Parking sensors do not prevent hitching a trailer.

1lzq0l9.q: Towing a trailer does not increase fuel consumption if one drives at moderate speed.
1lzq0l9.why: A trailer adds weight and air resistance, so fuel consumption rises even at moderate speed.

393hen.q: The moving mechanical parts of the towing devices of a motor vehicle and a trailer must be kept clean and properly lubricated.
393hen.why: The moving parts of towing gear must be kept clean and well lubricated.

15wmqgq.q: The towing devices of a vehicle must not show play, deformation or cracks.
15wmqgq.why: Towing gear must have no play, deformation or cracks, to keep the connection safe.

13il6e2.q: The towing devices of a vehicle must allow sufficient vertical oscillation between the towing vehicle and trailer, so as to compensate for the different inclinations of the vehicles due to uneven road surfaces.
13il6e2.why: Towing gear allows vertical movement that compensates for different tilts of the two vehicles on uneven roads.

zes8cp.q: When towing a trailer, check that the vertical load on the hitch does not exceed the limit indicated by the manufacturer.
zes8cp.why: The vertical load on the hitch must not exceed the manufacturer's limit.

1qgvqoh.q: The maximum vertical load that may bear on the towing vehicle's hitch is shown on a special plate fixed to the tow hitch.
1qgvqoh.why: The maximum vertical hitch load is stated on a plate fixed to the tow hitch.

sij03q.q: The towing devices of a vehicle do not need lubrication, but must be periodically degreased with special detergents or with petrol.
sij03q.why: Towing gear must be lubricated, not stripped of grease with detergents or petrol.

dpae2k.q: The towing devices of a vehicle may be non-type-approved if intended only for towing light trailers.
dpae2k.why: Towing gear must always be type-approved, even for light trailers.

17stjbq.q: To tow a light trailer, it is not necessary to make the electrical connection between the towing vehicle and the trailer.
17stjbq.why: The electrical connection is always needed so the trailer's lights and signals work.

xf9dmp.q: If the towing devices of a vehicle break, they may be repaired by welding at a specialised workshop.
xf9dmp.why: Broken towing gear must be replaced with type-approved parts, not repaired by welding.

1jwl6a6.q: The driver of a vehicle with a trailer must arrange the transported goods so that, while driving, there is no shifting, tipping over, falling or rubbing.
1jwl6a6.why: The load must be secured so it cannot shift, tip, fall off or rub during the journey.

14ru0gn.q: If a trailer is left inactive for a long time, it is advisable, if it cannot be lifted off the ground, to increase the tyre pressure and periodically change their contact surface, so as to avoid them becoming out of round.
14ru0gn.why: If a stored trailer stays on the ground, raise the tyre pressure and shift the contact point to prevent flat spots.

179bc1i.q: If the trailer remains inactive for a long time, it is advisable, if possible, to keep the tyres off the ground by placing supports under the chassis.
179bc1i.why: For long storage, lift the tyres off the ground with supports under the chassis.

1eei3nn.q: When towing a trailer, the inflation pressure of the towing vehicle's tyres must be the same as that of the trailer's tyres.
1eei3nn.why: Each vehicle has its own manufacturer-specified tyre pressure, and the two can differ.
